note: Seed list for the first citation audit (queue p13), built 2026-11-16 by hand from web search and direct page reads (WebFetch) for SEO-STRATEGY.md section 8: roundups and listicles of Quran, Islamic and Muslim apps for iPhone. Qualitative only (public repo). quranwall_present was judged from the page read, not a raw-HTML grep; none of the pages mentions QuranWall or any Quran Lock Screen / widget app. No contact has been made, no email or form was sent. Dropped after checking, so the next audit does not repeat the work: halalop.com (the roundup URL 301-redirects to a mitamina.com contact page), productivemuslim.com (the iPhone-apps article is from 2010), technicalustad.com/best-islamic-apps (2022, no update date), igeeksblog.com best azan apps page (HTTP 410), macmyths.com 10-best-quran-apps (the sister NoteWall audit found its own pages say positions are paid), techcabal.com and appshunter.io (HTTP 403 to automated reads; unverified), theculturetrip.com (read timed out; unverified), ar-pay.com (a gift-card vendor's blog). Search results also showed roundups published by app vendors ranking their own products (qissahapp.com, niyatapp.com, muslimnow.app, qurangate.app, fiveprayer.app): not read, not pitch targets. Re-run and refresh this file each time a citation-audit item executes; feeds p14 and p15 (outreach-prep).
core_query_set: quran verse on iphone lock screen

targets.contact_route: Contact Us page, a comment form under the article, and a WhatsApp 'Ask a Question' link on the page. No explicit app-submission or tips form is visible.
targets.angle: 'The 10 Best Quran Apps in 2026: Tested & Compared' (published 2026-01-01, updated 2026-08-08) covers ten reading, hifz and study apps and a 'New & Notable' list; none is a Lock Screen or widget app. Pitch the missing category (a verse on the Lock Screen you see every time you pick up the phone) with a reviewer offer code and the plain note that QuranWall is not a reading or memorisation tool.
targets.notes: Read directly via WebFetch. Not independent of commercial interests: the site is operated by Dr Ali Rajabi, who sells a memorisation course, and a reply in the comments refers to 'our own application' (not among the ten reviewed). The page states no app paid for placement. Pitch only for editorial evaluation, never for a paid slot.

targets.contact_route: Site Contact page (ioshacker.com/contact) and a Tips page (ioshacker.com/tips), both linked from the page footer/navigation. No explicit review-request invitation.
targets.angle: 'Best Azan And Prayer Times Apps For iPhone In 2026' (published and last updated 2026-02-19, bylined) lists six prayer-time apps and no Quran verse or Lock Screen app. This is an adjacent page, so the angle is the site rather than the page: an iOS-tips outlet that covers Lock Screen apps could take a short note on a Quran verse widget; use the Tips page, one message.
